data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject rather than describes it when the test's own acceptance criteria are satisfied by the installation procedure rather than by the subject's independent properties, and the 3-of-26 result is the set of mutations that the acceptance criteria never evaluated.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the acceptance criteria explicitly require evaluation of all mutations regardless of installation order, then the tautology is not present.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the 1/9 mutation was caught by a different test in the suite but not by compile.py specifically, then the loss is localized and not a general constraint.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the acceptance criteria were written before the shown-to-fail-first procedure was adopted, then the procedure is not the source of the constraint.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The compile.py test under shown-to-fail-first installation accepted a state that already contained the failure as its 'pass' condition. The acceptance criteria were therefore tautological: the test passed because the installation procedure guaranteed that the failure would be present before the test ran. This constrained the subject by making the test's outcome a function of the installation order rather than of the subject's code. The 1/9 mutation lost under compile.py was one that the acceptance criteria did not evaluate; the 3-of-26 distribution reflects the number of mutations whose effects were not observable under the installation-first regime.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
